reason: The separator needs a way to reject heat, and steel and coolant tubing suggest a radiator assembly.
expectation: The steel and tubing will form a heat-rejection component for the separator.

alternatives.reason: I could check its compatible parts first, but the cooling components suggest a direct combination.

effect: The cooling panel provides the heat-rejection path the separator needs.
reaction: The specified thermal contact and uncovered radiating surface make the assembly satisfying.
reason: The separator has open coolant connections, so the new cooling panel should connect to it.
expectation: The panel will provide cooling for the separator's condenser.

effect: The separator now has cooling but still needs a gas feed.
reaction: The separate coolant and process circuits are clear.
reason: The test cylinder contains the methane and water vapour the cooled separator is meant to process.
expectation: The test gas will pass through the cooled separator, allowing water to be collected.

effect: The test cylinder has no available operation, so it is not the separator's feed connection.
reaction: That was an unexpected dead end.
reason: Inspecting the cooled separator should reveal how to connect its process inlet.
expectation: The inspection will identify an available connection, possibly to the reactor.

alternatives.reason: The reactor may feed the separator directly, but the failed test-cylinder attempt makes checking useful.

effect: The separator is connected to the reactor outlet; the remaining task is likely to route recovered water.
reaction: The direct reactor connection makes sense now.
reason: The clean service hose is the available part suited to returning recovered water.
expectation: The hose will connect the separator's water return.

effect: The recovered water now returns to treatment, and the remaining goal is to feed clean methane from the reactor.
reaction: The separate water-return route is a useful detail.
reason: The available destination for clean methane is not clear, so I will check the reactor's connections.
expectation: The inspection will identify an available partner for the clean methane outlet.

effect: The inspection automatically processed the test batch through the connected installation and completed the clean-methane goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the test gas finally used, though its earlier incompatibility was surprising.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the cooled separator to the reactor was most worthwhile: it clarified the actual gas path and explained how water, methane and unreacted gas are handled.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to connect the test cylinder directly to the separator was a dead end; its brief feedback did not explain why the connection was unavailable.

surprise.text: The test cylinder could not be used with the cooled separator alone, but became usable after the reactor and water return were connected.

arbitrary.text: The cylinder's initial incompatibility felt somewhat arbitrary until the completed installation provided a route for processing its contents.

continue.text: I would continue: the physically explained cooling and water recovery made assembling the fuel plant interesting, and I would want to see how the return unfolds.
